zoe_customer: Hey support — one of our customers reports streaming responses get abruptly cut when users switch from their home WiFi to a phone hotspot. They see partial JSON/chunks and then connection closed. Happens ~3/5 times while switching networks.

erin_support: Sorry about that. Do you have a request_id or sample client logs? Any pattern on client OS/browser?

zoe_customer: request_id=rid_8f3a7b. Repro'd on Android Chrome and iOS Safari while user toggles hotspot on. Client logs show ECONNRESET and then SSE 'closed' event. No 4xx/5xx from our side in the app logs.

mike_oncall: Pasting server-side excerpt for rid_8f3a7b we grabbed: 
```
[2150001234.112] connection accepted; rid=rid_8f3a7b
[2150001240.451] streaming tokens: 0..78
[2150001241.002] write to socket failed: broken pipe
[2150001241.003] client disconnect: remote close
```
Looks like server did a final write and socket reset. Could be client or an intermediary (NAT/gateway) abort.

lisa_engineer: Two quick suspects: (1) client-side TCP/TLS session tear during network change, (2) idle timeouts on an intermediary (mobile carrier NAT, CF/ALB) closing connection when network path changes.

nate_network: Also check load balancer idle timeout + proxy TCP re-use. If the client IP changes midstream the backend sees a different 5-tuple and the existing socket gets killed. Mobile hotspots often cause NAT rebinding.

erin_support: OK. Customer wants repro steps to share with their mobile team. Can we provide a minimal curl/node repro and recommended mitigations/workarounds?

lisa_engineer: Minimal curl can't easily simulate a network switch mid-request, but here's how to reproduce server behavior locally: start a long-running stream then forcibly close the TCP connection from client side after a delay to mirror a network flip. Example using socat / curl.

mike_oncall: Also adding a snippet for clients to detect and gracefully retry streams: if you see partial data + 'close' event, record last good token index and restart request with the same prompt. Append a note: server does not currently support stream-resume at token granularity, so client must re-request and dedupe.

lisa_engineer: Suggested immediate mitigations for customer: 
- Add a short heartbeat comment every 10s from server to keep connection alive (e.g. SSE ":\n" keepalive lines).
- Configure client SDK to not abort the fetch immediately on transient network events; add exponential reconnect with jitter.
- Check any corporate/proxy/mobile carrier idle timeouts and raise them (often 30–60s).
- If possible, prefer small non-streaming responses for flaky mobile networks.

nate_network: Action items for us: collect packet capture (pcap) from the client's device during repro (or at least TCP stats / syslogs), full server logs around rid_8f3a7b, and load balancer / edge logs showing flow teardown reasons.

erin_support: Zoe — would you be able to get a pcap or tcpdump from the user when they repro? If not, ask their mobile/dev team for the network operator and any proxy info. We'll open an escalation ticket on our side.

zoe_customer: I'll ask them for a pcap and the carrier info. They can repro reliably in ~10 attempts. Thanks for the heartbeat tip.

mike_oncall: Temporary workaround we gave other customers: send a tiny comment frame every 8–12s so any middlebox sees traffic and keeps mapping open. Example SSE keepalive line: `:\n` (a single colon followed by newline).

lisa_engineer: Also check token TTL: if token refresh happens midstream it can cause client SDKs to re-initiate connections incorrectly. Confirm their auth token TTL is > expected stream duration.

nate_network: Logging note: we should add an alert that correlates 'write to socket failed' with client IP change in the same timeframe. Filing SI-4521 for this pattern.

deploy-bot: deploy: edge-proxy hotfix candidate pushed to canary (edge-timeout-adjustment) by lisa_engineer at 2150001290

erin_support: Great. I'll create the escalation (SI-4521) and email the customer the mitigation steps + request pcap. Will update here when we get the pcap or load balancer logs.

zoe_customer: Thanks — forwarding to their mobile infra team now.

lisa_engineer: If they can capture a quick Chrome bug repro: open devtools -> Network, start stream, toggle hotspot, watch for "net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET" and save HAR. HAR + pcap is the most actionable.

mike_oncall: Summary for the customer: likely not Redwood server intentionally closing stream. Most probable causes: NAT rebinding / TLS session break / LB idle timeout / client abort. Recommended: heartbeat, client retry, check proxies, capture pcap/har.

erin_support: Closing loop — once we have pcap + lb logs we'll validate and either implement an edge timeout tweak or recommend a permanent SDK heartbeat.

zoe_customer: Will follow up. Appreciated.
